newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar bounces back after two-day break.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar bounces back after two-day break.

text.p: Indian sugar prices bounced back on Friday after a two-day holiday break on renewed consumer buying and fresh interest, dealers said.

They said fresh offerings were also scattered since millers had sold most sugar stocks out of the current month's free sale quota. Ready delivery S-30 sugar rose by five rupees to 1,245/1,285 rupees per quintal and M-30 rose by 5/10 rupees to 1,275/1,330. The markets were closed on Wednesday and Thursday.
"The market recovered today but sentiment is still not encouraging in view of a higher free sale quota next month," one dealer said. Next month's free sale quota is 850,000 tonnes.
